subject: MedTech Global — DPF & export controls: technical evidence request
summary: MedTech Global requested supplemental evidence for cross-border controls and DPF alignment. Redwood provided a technical evidence pack, diagrams, KMS/HSM details, and a row-by-row DPA Annex mapping. Thread includes follow-up clarifications and a final delivery link and DocuSign reference.
messages:
From: Sarah Hall <sarah.hall@medtechglobal.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medtechglobal.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0500
Subject: MedTech — request: DPF evidence and export controls details

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the overview in last week's call. We need a compact technical package to satisfy our privacy & procurement teams before we proceed to procurement. Specifically we need:

- A mapping of cross-border flows (which services/regions process customer data and any third-party subprocessors);
- Evidence of controls that satisfy the US–EU DPF technical measures (pseudonymization, encryption in transit & at rest, KMS practices, key separation for multi-tenant workloads);
- The DPA Annex mapping that shows where Redwood's standard terms map to our Annex clauses (we provided sample clause numbers in the attached RFI);
- Any HSM/KMS attestations or SOC-type artifacts that you can share for the hosted service (redacted as necessary).

Can you get a consolidated package and a short point-by-point response to the items in the attached RFI (MedTech_RFI_20261116.pdf)? Ideally by EOD Wednesday (Nov 18) so our legal team can review before the Friday internal packet. If you'd prefer a 30-minute follow-up instead of the doc, happy to book.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Hall
Head of Data Privacy, MedTech Global

--- attachment: MedTech_RFI_20261116.pdf (8 pages)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Hall <sarah.hall@medtechglobal.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MedTech — request: DPF evidence and export controls details

Hi Sarah — thanks, and appreciate the clear ask. We're preparing a concise evidence pack and a row-level DPA Annex mapping per your attachment. High-level responses below; full attachments are in the zip I will send in a follow-up: redwood_dpf_evidence_pack_v1.zip.

1) Cross-border flows:
- Primary control plane and metadata services for hosted API are in us-east-1 and us-west-2 for US customers; customer data persistence occurs in the region you choose (we support region-pin to EU or US for Dedicated/Private). For hosted accounts with EU-region selection, data is stored in eu-west-1 with a strict egress policy.
- Subprocessor list (high level): AWS (storage/compute), GCP (replication for specific managed regions), FastLayer CDN (edge for low-latency streaming). Detailed mapping is in export-dataflow-diagram.png.

2) DPF technical measures (summary):
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.3 with mutual auth for internal service-to-service; customer-facing endpoints use ALB with enforced TLS.
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 across block volumes and S3, with envelope encryption managed by customer-specific KMS keys where requested.
- Key management: KMS-backed keys; for Dedicated/Private customers we offer customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-KMS or HSM-backed keys. KMS rotation policy: 90-day automatic rotation with asymmetrical master keys rotated via HSM-backed signing (see kms-key-rotation-and-hsm-summary.pdf).
- Pseudonymization: configurable output redaction and tokenization via the runtime; also prefix/KV caching uses per-customer namespaces.

3) DPA Annex mapping: We're prepping a row-by-row mapping to your Annex clause numbers — that will be dpa-annex-mapping.xlsx in the packet.

4) Attestations & evidence: We cannot publish raw SOC reports for hosted customers but can provide redacted evidence and an HSM summary; see the attached PDF. If you need a tighter NDA and controlled share, let us know and we can route through our legal team.

If this looks right I'll send the zip now and propose a 30-minute technical walkthrough Tuesday/Wednesday to run through any gaps.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
--- attachment: redwood_dpf_evidence_pack_v1.zip (contains the items listed above)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Sarah Hall <sarah.hall@medtechglobal.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MedTech — request: DPF evidence and export controls details

Sarah / team — adding a short technical supplement and the export-dataflow-diagram.png for clarity (attached). Notes: 

- Dataflow summary: customer input (ingest API) -> region-local inference pool (pinned where requested) -> KV/prefix cache (encrypted, per-customer key namespace) -> optional cross-region replication for DR (only enabled with explicit customer consent). The diagram marks where we encrypt and boundary points for subprocessors.
- Subprocessors: we include subprocessors in the diagram with the processing purpose; for any subprocessor that introduces cross-border transfer we list contractual controls in the mapping file.
- HSM usage: for hosted customers on enterprise tier we keep master keys in HSM; the HSM provider supports FIPS 140-2 Level 3 and gives attestation APIs. We included a short summary (kms-key-rotation-and-hsm-summary.pdf) listing rotation cadence, split-key procedures, and emergency key compromise playbook.

Call to action: if MedTech needs an HSM attestation under NDA, we'll kick off a controlled share.

Thanks — attaching: export-dataflow-diagram.png, kms-key-rotation-and-hsm-summary.pdf

Ben
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Hall <sarah.hall@medtechglobal.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medtechglobal.com, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MedTech — request: DPF evidence and export controls details

Marissa / Ben — thank you, the packet is helpful. A few follow-ups from Legal and Privacy: 

- We need a row-level mapping in the XLS that explicitly references our Annex clause numbers (10.1 — cross-border guarantee; 12.4 — pseudonymization; 18.2 — logging/retention). Your preliminary mapping is fine but please add column references to the specific controls/evidence files (e.g., point to kms-key-rotation-and-hsm-summary.pdf row 3).
- We require a statement on whether Redwood ever performs tenant co-mingling at storage layer for hosted customers (we define co-mingling as using shared buckets with tenant identifiers vs dedicated buckets). Please confirm the default behavior and whether dedicated buckets can be requested.
- For DR cross-region replication: please confirm if customer data is replicated automatically or only when explicitly enabled.
- Finally, we need an HSM attestation or a redacted extract for the hosted service (enterprise tier) as mentioned. If available under NDA, please indicate the expected turnaround.

Thanks — target for internal review is Friday EOD; if you can update the XLS and confirm these points today/tomorrow that will help.

Best,
Sarah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Hall <sarah.hall@medtechglobal.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MedTech — request: DPF evidence and export controls details

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clarifying questions, apologies for the rapid fire. Answers below and pointers to updated artifacts (attached/uploaded):

1) Row-level mapping: updated dpa-annex-mapping.xlsx with explicit references to files and line items (column G points to filenames and sheet tabs).

2) Tenant co-mingling: default hosted behavior uses logical isolation (per-tenant namespaces within shared storage) — metadata and object keys include tenant namespace; data blocks may reside on shared S3 buckets for efficiency but are encrypted with per-tenant envelope keys. Dedicated buckets and dedicated storage are available on request (typically part of Dedicated/Private engagements).

3) Cross-region replication / DR: replication is NOT automatic by default. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature requiring configuration during onboarding or via support request; replication only occurs with explicit consent and is logged in the tenant audit trail.

4) HSM attestation: we can provide a redacted attestation extract for the hosted Enterprise tier under NDA. Typical turnaround after NDA is 5–7 business days to coordinate with our HSM provider and legal team. If MedTech needs a full HSM report or onsite review, we can scope that as a separate item.

Deliverables: uploaded package to the shared Drive link and attached the updated XLS and a one-page summary PDF. Also filed a HubSpot deal note: MTG-2026-09. If you prefer, we can route an NDA for the attestation today and start the HSM share process.

Next step: do you want the NDA routed to legal@redwood.com or to Ben's team for an expedited flow?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
